newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes higher, trades narrow range.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes higher, trades narrow range.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed higher on Friday after trading in a 26 basis point range against the U.S. dollar on the day.
The kiwi closed at US$0.7081/88 after opening at 0.7070/75.
On the Trade Weighted Index the kiwi closed up 28 basis points at 67.57.
Dealers said selling out of Asia and buying against the Australian dollar were the main drivers with a quiet day in politics and the release of employment numbers having little impact.

Nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power, is negotiating with the caretaker conservative National government and the main opposition Labour party after the inconclusive general election on October 12.
The parties finished formal negotiations for the week on Thursday and resume on Tuesday.

Stronger than expected jobs growth of 0.8 percent in the September quarter intially surprised the markets, but closer inspection showed all the growth was in part time jobs while full time job numbers fell 0.8 percent.
"The kiwi whipped around in a small range of 0.7070 to 0.7096," an Auckland-based bank dealer said.
"Good selling was seen out of Asia throughout the day but there was a lot of buying of the kiwi against the Aussie during the course of the day."
He said it was not as busy as the hectic trading on Thursday.
Overnight dealers saw the kiwi trading in a range between 0.7060 and 0.7090 with a base forming around 0.7040.
